messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: missing data and stan
parts:
This is probably a topic for stan 2.0, but am I correct in thinking
that stan 1.x has no concept of doing full-Bayesian inference with
missing data. I think this is possible with BUGS, so I just didn't
want the initial design of stan to make adding such a feature too hard
in the future.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] missing data and stan
parts:
Any missing data model in BUGS can be
translated into Stan 1. I've gone over how to
do it in past e-mails and on Andrew's board
and will include examples in the doc.

The basic idea is to break the vector of data
into missing and non-missing parts and then
duplicate code. Ugly for the repetitious code,
but it works in general.

The problem with directly translating the BUGS
models is that Stan doesn't allow mixed vectors
of data and parameters. The types, double and
stan::agrad::var, don't mix. We can't fix the
value of a parameter given the way HMC works.

After breaking them out, you can put them
back together into a transformed parameter vector
or matrix. For instance, you might want to do this
if the missing "data" is an entry in a covariance
matrix some of whose entries are known.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: missing data and stan
parts:
OK, that is really good. I'll watch the commits for an example of how
to do a model like that.

For the special case of covariance matrices with known entries, I
should probably write a non-ugly dedicated mechanism. In the canoncial
partial correlations framework, fixing the i-j regular correlation
implies a nonlinear constraint (that we would have to solve) on the i-
j CPC and the triangularity of the Jacobian implies that these only
affect "downstream" correlations. Basically, we can just reduce the
number of free (primitive parameters underlying the) CPCs by the
number of constraints on the regular correlations and proceed.
However, it may be the case that for some values of the known and free
parameters, there is no solution for the fixed CPC on the (-1,1)
interval, which we would have to deal with somehow.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] missing data and stan
parts:
I think Stan can do full Bayes with missing data but as I recall there is some sort of hack needed to put together the full matrix from the observed and missing pieces.

When we discussed this a few months ago, I think we were talking about ultimately coding this hack as some sort of function/subroutine. But Bob would know more.

A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: missing data and stan
parts:
Currently in bugs_examples, we have some missing data, at least
in the original data, we have NA's. 

vol1/mice and vol1/kidney:
missing data are specifically censored data. 
What I did is following what Bob said: splitting them
and modeling accordingly. 

vol2/cervix:
missing data are modeled as parameters if missing
though this example could not run since 
the missing ones are discrete. 

--
Jiqiang
